name: dns-doctor
description: Scan, fix and verify a domain's DNS: email authentication (SPF, DMARC, DKIM), multi-region propagation, SPF include supply-chain audits, MX, DNS health, blacklists and domain/SSL expiry. Returns deterministic verdicts and copy-paste fix records generated by a validating engine — never a guessed record.

interface.shortDescription: Scan, fix and verify a domain's DNS — SPF, DMARC, DKIM, propagation, DNS health, blacklists, expiry.
interface.longDescription: DNS Doctor scans, fixes and verifies a domain's DNS and returns deterministic verdicts plus copy-paste fix records generated by a validating engine (RFC grammar plus the SPF 10-lookup counter) — never an LLM guess. It diagnoses email authentication (SPF, DMARC, DKIM), MX, DNS health, blacklist listings, and domain/SSL expiry; audits who can transitively send as a domain through its SPF includes; verifies from six vantage points whether a DNS change has propagated globally; builds evidence-gated DMARC enforcement upgrades (capped at p=quarantine, and only when the server-derived alignment gate passes — p=reject comes from aggregate-report evidence, never from a scan); and hands the human a sign-up link to start free DMARC monitoring — nothing is created until they sign in there themselves. A human approves every DNS change.
defaultPrompt: Scan my domain for email authentication problems and explain anything that is failing.
Mail from my domain keeps landing in spam — diagnose it and give me the exact DNS records to fix.
Is it safe to move my domain's DMARC policy to enforcement? If yes, give me the record to publish.
